critical_code_review_comments: SECURITY FIX 1 correctly applied to all 3 cookie-issuing endpoints (register L225, login L264, session-exchange L362). Regex scan of server.py confirms 0 remaining samesite="none". Same-origin frontend flow is unaffected by Lax (dashboard, /api/auth/me, POST purchase all work).

SECURITY FIX 2 helper _resolve_safe_origin (L925) is correctly gated: (a) rejects non-http(s) schemes via prefix check, (b) exact-matches against CORS_ORIGINS env var, (c) regex-matches against CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX (defaults to '^https://[a-z0-9-]+\.preview\.emergentagent\.com$' — anchored ^...$ so suffix attacks fail), (d) falls back to str(request.base_url) which is backend-derived and safe by construction. Called at L993 replacing the previous naive `purchase.origin_url or str(request.base_url)`.

The default CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX correctly uses `\.preview\.emergentagent\.com$` with a trailing $ anchor, so 'evil.preview.emergentagent.com.attacker.com' does NOT match — confirmed by test_resolve_safe_origin_rejects_suffix_attack.

rca of the issue: No new issues found. Both fixes are correctly applied. RCA of original security issues: (1) SameSite=None allowed the session cookie to be attached on cross-site subrequests, expanding CSRF exposure without any legitimate cross-site use case (frontend is same-origin) — mitigation: SameSite=Lax on all 3 cookie-setting endpoints. (2) purchase.origin_url was directly reflected into Stripe success_url/cancel_url — an attacker who tricks a user into calling the endpoint with a crafted origin_url could redirect the user to attacker.com after payment (CWE-601 Open Redirect). Mitigation: _resolve_safe_origin() validates the candidate against CORS_ORIGINS allowlist + CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX (anchored, so suffix attacks fail), only accepts http(s) schemes (blocking javascript:/data:/protocol-relative), and falls back to backend-derived request.base_url when the candidate is unsafe.
